scope: One bounded Linux synthetic journal locking audit; no statistical computation or real user journals.

scenarios.writer: test probe holding the actual production coordination lock while pausing after the first byte of a synthetic JSON entry
scenarios.expected: reader waits for writer, then reads one complete entry
JOURNAL_UNREADABLE failure, not successful empty journal
actual reader waits across an OS-session boundary, then reads the complete entry
terminate only the owned paused synthetic writer; reader acquires released file lock and reports retained partial JSON as JOURNAL_UNREADABLE
reader fails explicitly after the 10-second lock deadline; no unsafe fallback or corruption verdict

invariants: Exact deterministic writer IDs, no lost or duplicate entries
Every previous hash equals SHA256 of the exact preceding UTF8 line
No premature corruption finding during a mutex-protected cooperative write
Persistent malformed data still fails closed
Finite watchdogs and preserved failures; no stress loop or tuning
limits: Synthetic large-entry overlap is a controlled integrity test, not a normal workload estimate
Named-lock cooperation does not protect against arbitrary external file editors or authenticate the journal
